transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-20 15:00 PT | Duration: 68m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Miles (Redwood CS), Lucas (CTO - Medisync), Aisha (Lead ML Eng), Tom (Infra), Sara (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya our SE. Miles is on for any procurement questions. Medisync, do you want to intro real quick?
[00:12] Lucas: Yeah hi, Lucas here, CTO. We're trying to reduce inference spend while keeping high fidelity on clinical summarization. Aisha will lead the model work.
[00:20] Aisha: Hey all. We're especially worried about hallucinations in compressed models and latency under 250ms tail for patient-facing flows.
[00:28] Priya: Great, that's helpful. Today we'll demo the Optimize Console playbook for hybrid quantization — how we pick int8 profiles for cheaper bulk workloads, fp8 for fidelity-critical endpoints, and routing/fallback policies. We'll also propose a 48-hour sandbox run.
[00:42] Tom: Quick security note, we need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration details, and the option for a VPC/private deploy.
[00:48] Jordan: Totally, we'll share the security pack and SSO docs after.

[01:10] Priya: Okay jumping into the Console — I'm sharing my screen, can everyone see the Optimize -> Quant Profiles page? (screen flicker)
[01:22] Sara: We can see it.
[01:25] Priya: Cool. So on the left is your model catalog, we've onboarded a gpt-ish open model - in console it shows baseline perf numbers. The Q-profiles are precomputed: "safety-first-fp8", "balanced-int8", and "throughput-int8-aggressive". Note the profile metrics are generated from our eval harness — tokens-per-second, avg latency, and a quality delta score.
[01:46] Aisha: That quality delta, what's the baseline? Like, is it measured against FP16 full precision?
[01:51] Priya: Yes, baseline is FP16 — in our system we compute BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxies plus a domain-specific hallucination metric when customers provide evals. I should flag that the proxies are noisy for clinical text — that's why we want you to provide your prompt set.
[02:10] Lucas: When you say kv cache behavior changes with int8, what do you mean? We've seen weird token drift in other runtimes.
[02:17] Priya: Right — so quantization affects kernel math and marginal logits sometimes. Also how the runtime serializes/keeps the KV cache (we do prefix caching and a warm-cache path) can interact with int8 leading to small divergence on long contexts. In practice we see drift subword-level after many tokens; we surface that in the "cache-delta" metric.
[02:40] Tom: That's the "kv cash" I've been worried about — I think some transcription on earlier calls said 'kv cash' haha.
[02:46] [laughter]

[03:10] Priya: Here's a quick perf table — balanced-int8 reduces token cost ~2.8x vs fp16, with median latency improvement 1.6x, and quality delta -1.8 (on our proxy). fp8 often gives a better quality-latency sweet spot: ~1.9x cost reduction with only -0.6 quality delta in many of our medical evals. That said, fp8 is hardware-dependent — some older GPUs don't have efficient fp8 paths.
[03:40] Aisha: Which hardware are you targeting for fp8? We're on A100s in prod and considering H100 for bursts.
[03:47] Priya: H100s are ideal for fp8; A100 has limited fp8 perf. In Dedicated or Private you can pin instance types. For Hosted we will route to the best available variant but we also show a model-variant perf profile.

[04:10] Jordan: One key pattern we recommend is a hybrid routing policy: route patient-facing summarization to fp8 or full-precision canary; route batch analytics to aggressive int8. Then use our per-prompt tagging or per-route headers to pick profiles.
[04:25] Lucas: Can we do per-customer or per-route SLO overrides? E.g., low latency but very high fidelity for certain clinics?
[04:32] Priya: Yes, we support per-route configs in the Console. You can pin a route to a Q-profile and set fallback policies — for example, if fp8 fails or quality regression is detected it falls back to FP16 on a percentage of samples.

[05:00] Aisha: About regressions — how do you detect a quality regression in production? We can't label everything.
[05:06] Priya: Good question. Our Quality Monitor ties into your prompt sets and expected outputs (you can seed it with 100 eval prompts). We compute statistical drift and a hallucination score; if the delta exceeds thresholds we'll trigger alerts and can automatically reduce traffic to a safer profile. We also sample outputs for human review.
[05:24] Sara: Is there an SDK hook for capturing the evaluation feedback? We want to maintain a closed loop.
[05:29] Priya: Yep, there's a small SDK and webhook. We'll include the snippet in the playbook.

[06:00] Jordan: Let's run a quick demo of a latency vs quality sweep. Priya, can you kick off the Sandbox runner?
[06:07] Priya: Kicking it now. I'm running three profiles concurrently — fp16 baseline, balanced-int8, and fp8-balanced. The runner will push your sample prompts (I used a synthetic clinical set for demo). Starting the live logs...
[06:30] [screen share logs] Priya: You can see median p50/p95 latency per profile, and a small plot of quality delta vs latency. Balanced-int8 has p95 ~ 320ms in this cloud region, fp8 p95 ~ 210ms on H100, fp16 p95 ~ 480ms. But quality delta for balanced-int8 is -2.4 on the proxy, fp8 is -0.8.
[07:00] Aisha: Proxy metrics are one thing, but could we run a head-to-head with our annotators? We'll need that to sign off.
[07:07] Jordan: Absolutely — that's why we propose the 48-hour sandbox using your real prompts. Priya will provision it and we'll run both automated and human-in-the-loop checks.

[07:30] Tom: Network-wise, how do you measure e2e latency? Our infra will have VPN and NAT egress that adds variability.
[07:38] Priya: The sandbox captures e2e latency from your environment if you run the client from your network; otherwise we give a region-to-region baseline. We can instrument with distributed traces — the Console shows token-level timing and where time is spent: network, queuing, compute kernels.
[08:00] Lucas: On routing — can Redwood pause a profile rollout automatically if hallucination rate climbs?
[08:06] Priya: Yes, we have an automated rollback policy in the Rollouts tab: you can set health checks and quality thresholds. If the metric breaches, traffic is rerouted to fallback.

[08:30] Aisha: Are there known edge cases where int8 is strictly unusable? We had a case with numeric reasoning where states broke.
[08:37] Priya: Numeric-heavy tasks and long-form generation are more sensitive. We usually recommend fp8 or full-precision for those. Also certain attention patterns in variants of code-gen or heavily tokenized clinical identifiers can magnify errors.

[09:10] [10-minute mark discussion on benchmarks, then jump]
[10:45] Priya: I want to call out the Q-profile metadata — it includes a "sensitivity tag" we auto-assign. You can override tags so the ConsoleWill automatically avoid aggressive profiles on tagged routes.
[10:59] Lucas: How invasive is integration with our KMS? We need each token stored encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys.
[11:06] Jordan: For Private or Dedicated, we support KMS/HSM integrations; for Hosted, we have envelope encryption with optional customer-managed KMS for certain enterprise tiers. We'll attach the security integration doc.
[11:20] Tom: Any audit log retention limits? We have regulatory retention needs for a year.
[11:26] Miles: Audit logs and request/response retention is configurable in Enterprise plans; there are add-on retention packages. We'll include pricing.

[12:00] Aisha: Back to the perf numbers — can you show token throughput for batch analytics use-case?
[12:06] Priya: Sure, switching to batch. For throughput-int8-aggressive we get ~3.5x token throughput vs fp16 with slightly worse quality deltas, but it's excellent for non-customer-facing backfills.
[12:25] Lucas: So recommended pattern: non-sensitive batch to aggressive int8, patient-facing to fp8 or fp16 with canary rollouts and monitoring.
[12:33] Jordan: Exactly. And the Console has traffic-splitting controls so you can do 5% canary with auto-evaluate.

[13:00] [short pause, customer side confers]
[13:25] Aisha: For the 48-hour sandbox, what do you need from us?
[13:29] Priya: Two representative prompt sets (patient summaries + structured extraction), a small gold set for evaluation (~200 samples), and an endpoint or test client running from your network if you want true e2e latency. Also any specific thresholds for hallucination or latency.
[13:45] Jordan: We'll also send a simple onboarding checklist and the playbook link. Deck: "Hybrid Quantization Playbook" (shared).

[14:20] Tom: Regarding private deployment — if we go on-prem, can we run the same Console or is that split?
[14:27] Priya: Our Private offering has a control plane option — you can either have a managed control plane with VPC peering or a customer-managed plane. The Console is available as a customer-facing UI; in fully air-gapped environments we provide an on-prem console bundle. There is some feature parity caveat on auto-routing to hosted fallbacks.

[15:00] Jordan: Let's surface common objections — cost vs latency. Typically customers trade a modest quality delta for big cost wins, but for critical flows we recommend conservative profiles and sampling. Any other concerns?
[15:14] Lucas: Vendor lock-in — if we tune heavily to Redwood profiles, how portable are those configs?
[15:20] Priya: Configs are exportable and the playbook documents how to translate to other runtimes, but runtime-specific kernels and fv will differ. We recommend keeping evals and the gold set as the source of truth.

[16:00] Aisha: Could we try a micro-pilot on a subset of clinics for 2 weeks instead? That might be more realistic than a 48-hour stress test.
[16:06] Jordan: We can do both: a 48-hour automated sandbox for fast perf numbers and a follow-up 2-week real-world micro-pilot on a single clinic.

[16:30] [customer asks pricing; Jordan answers high level]
[17:00] Jordan: Pricing — hosted pricing is usage-based with token tiers and reserved capacity discounts for Dedicated. For the micro-pilot we can provide credits and a temporary reserved slice. I'll send concrete numbers after this call.

[17:40] Aisha: One more technical: do you support mixed-precision within a single model during generation? Like dynamic fallback at token-level?
[17:48] Priya: We do not do token-level mixed precision dynamic switching today. We have sequence-level profiles and per-request profile selection. Token-level would add complexity to kernel orchestration and is on the research roadmap.

[18:30] [wrap-up and recap]
[18:40] Jordan: Quick recap: Redwood to share qprofile playbook, pricing, security docs. Priya to provision 48-hour sandbox with int8 and fp8 profiles using your prompt sets. Medisync to provide prompts, network info, and SLOs. Plan for micro-pilot once sandbox results are reviewed.
[18:58] Lucas: Sounds good. If the sandbox shows unacceptable hallucination on int8 we may default to fp8 for patient flows.
[19:05] Priya: Understood. We'll instrument sampling for human review.

[19:30] Miles: I'll follow up separately on contract terms and retention add-ons.
[19:36] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll send notes and next steps.
[19:45] Aisha: Thanks, bye.
[19:48] Lucas: Thanks all.
[19:50] End of meeting.

Notes (auto): Deck and playbook links shared in chat; logging artifacts: sandbox-run-001 (link). Some transcription artifacts around "KV cache" -> "kv cash".
